subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` as core lifecycle phases for sub-agent startup, or solve the startup-silence problem through a narrower existing-phase/status path?
rationale: The source-reproducible bug is real, but the proposed fix creates a new cross-surface lifecycle contract that affects gateway, SDK, session-state, and subagent consumers; automation should not choose that API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt the lifecycle contract
options.body: Implement `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` on current main with explicit gateway, SDK, session-state, and subagent tests plus proof for startup aborts.

options.title: Use existing terminal phases
options.body: Keep the public lifecycle phase set unchanged and encode startup failure through existing `error`/terminal metadata with stronger diagnostics and wait-state projection.

options.title: Pause until sandbox-specific proof
options.body: Defer the API decision until the sandboxed startup stall in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39248 has live proof that identifies whether a lifecycle contract or preflight rejection is the right product shape.

recommendation.title: Adopt the lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Implement `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` on current main with explicit gateway, SDK, session-state, and subagent tests plus proof for startup aborts.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history across subagent lifecycle and registry surfaces that anchor the product/API choice.
